results.correct_value: The 60 m caveat concerns pitch 3 (a 60 m rope may not stretch from the pitch-2 anchor to the true summit); the pitch-2 south-face rappel is a standard descent option with a single 60 m rope, with no stated rope-length problem.
results.evidence: The route's own description on Mountain Project says a 60 m rope may not make it to the true summit depending on where the anchor is set, and that the mellow terrain makes this a non-issue; it lists the rappel anchor on the south face at the pitch-2 belay as a descent without any rope caveat. The Mountaineers route page gives the same two descents (rappel the south face from the pitch-2 anchor, or over the summit and down the south scramble) with no rope-length warning, and the Mazamas trip page lists a single 60 m rope as the rope required. The 'rappel may not reach the ground' wording was a misreading of the pitch-3 note.

results.correct_value: From Pinnacle Saddle, Pinnacle Peak is to the east (Plummer is west); head east to the south-side gullies.
results.evidence: A Mountaineers/WTA trip report describes the path from Pinnacle Saddle going east toward the loose slopes and the summit gully, and says Plummer is reached by heading right (west) from the saddle. Visit Rainier's trail page says the path east from the saddle is the climbers' path to Pinnacle Peak. The beta's 'west/southwest' was the lone outlier against the approach, climbing_route and baseFinding.

results.correct_value: The standard route is the south gully / south face.
results.evidence: Wikipedia's Pinnacle Peak article gives the easiest route as a scramble of the south face; a hiking guide and trip reports describe the scramble as the south gully, mostly class 2 with a few class 3 moves. The row's aspect, name, face, approach and pro_tips already say south; three fields said north.

gain_ft 1,050 is the trailhead-to-saddle figure (NPS: 1,050 ft to the 5,920 ft saddle). The row's itinerary day gainFt, totalNote and the trailhead (4,870) and summit (6,562) waypoints all give ~1,700 ft to the summit. The Mazamas page for the same summit from the same trailhead states 1,700 ft; an Oregon Hikers report gives ~1,150 + ~600 ft and a hiking guide ~1,000 + 600 ft, bracketing it. loss_ft left unchanged per the loss rule (see discovered entry).
loss_ft 1,050 is the saddle-only figure while the itinerary day's lossFt is 1,700. No outside source states a car-to-car descent figure for this route, so loss_ft is left for review.

NPS gives 2.5 mi round trip to the saddle only (matching dist_km 2.1 km / 1.3 mi one way to the saddle and the itinerary's 2.6 mi). To the summit, a hiking guide says about 3 mi out and back, and an Oregon Hikers report says 1.3 mi to the saddle plus about 1/3 mi more to the top (~3.2-3.3 mi round trip). Both contradict the summit pin's 1.9 mi one way (3.8 RT), but they do not agree on one figure, and the intermediate pins' distances are unsourced; no patch.

Sources split: a hiking guide calls the south gully mostly class 2 with a few class 3 moves, a trip report calls the gully upper class 3, while an Oregon Hikers report describes class 3/4 scrambling and Wikipedia says some scrambling and rock climbing is needed. No two sources agree on a single maximum class that would settle the 4th Class pill versus the Class 2-3 descriptions, so no patch.
